summary.name: Treewise
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native Mac file manager that works like Windows Explorer, with a folder tree, address bar, cut and paste, and side-by-side windows.
keywords: cloud folder browser dropbox onedrive icloud
use_cases: Moving files between folders on a Mac the way Windows Explorer does
Renaming many files using patterns with dates and numbers
Creating a standard set of project or tax folders from a template
Browsing Dropbox, OneDrive and iCloud Drive folders without downloading them
Opening a folder in Terminal from a file manager window
summary.what_it_does: Treewise is a native macOS file manager aimed at people used to Windows Explorer. It shows a folder tree with favorites, disks, the home folder and cloud folders, plus an address bar with path buttons and a command bar with cut, copy, paste, rename and Move to Trash. Two windows can sit side by side, and cut/copy/paste works between windows and Finder, with undo for most operations. It can suggest file names from existing naming patterns (user approves each one) and create folder structures from saved templates, previewed before creation. Cloud files show a status icon and download only when opened, and it can open a folder in several terminal apps.
notable: Windows Explorer-style folder tree, address bar and cut/paste on macOS
Suggest Names proposes file names from existing patterns, approved one by one before renaming
Folder templates and Copy/Paste Folder Structure with a preview before creation
Signed and notarized by Apple; updates signed by Apple Developer ID and Treewise's own key
caveats: Name suggestions rely on add-ons that run in a separate service (no internet access, limited file data)
